Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Delegated legislation must stay within the limits set by the parent Act.
items.markingKey: (c) Delegated legislation must stay within the limits set by the parent Act.
options: It is made deliberately by a competent authority, is written, precise and can be changed quickly to meet new needs.
Under Article 51(c) and Article 253 India respects treaty obligations, and courts read conventions consistent with Fundamental Rights into domestic law.
Delegated legislation must stay within the limits set by the parent Act.
The legislature lacks the time and technical expertise to frame every detail and needs flexibility for emergencies.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about precedent as a source of law is NOT correct?
items.answer: The Supreme Court is bound by all its earlier decisions.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. The Supreme Court can depart from its earlier decisions, as held in Bengal Immunity (1955).
options: The Supreme Court is not bound by its own earlier decisions and can depart from them.
The Supreme Court is bound by all its earlier decisions.
The decisions of a High Court bind the subordinate courts within its territory.
Obiter dicta of the Supreme Court are given great weight by lower courts even though they are not strictly binding.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Courts refuse to enforce an immoral custom.
Reason (R): A custom can override a valid statute.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: A statute prevails over a conflicting custom.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In the study of other sources of law, the term 'Ijma' refers to:
items.answer: Consensus of Muslim jurists on a point of law
items.markingKey: (c) 'Ijma' means consensus of Muslim jurists on a point of law.
options: The doctrine of 'standing by things decided', under which courts follow earlier decisions
Legislation made by an authority other than the sovereign legislature, under power given by it
Consensus of Muslim jurists on a point of law
Beyond the powers given; a rule made beyond the powers of the parent Act is void

items.stem:
Read the following extract on precedent as a source of law and answer the questions that follow.
"A decision of a larger bench binds a smaller bench of the same court. Obiter dicta of the Supreme Court are given great weight by lower courts even though they are not strictly binding. Precedent brings certainty and consistency to the law."
(i) Under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'stare decisis' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The decisions of the Supreme Court bind all courts in India. (1)
items.answer: (i) all courts within the territory of India (ii) The doctrine of 'standing by things decided', under which courts follow earlier decisions. (iii) Article 141 declares that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) all courts within the territory of India (ii) The doctrine of 'standing by things decided', under which courts follow earlier decisions. (iii) Article 141 declares that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about legislation as a source of law:
I. Legislation is the most important source of law in modern states.
II. An ordinance can be issued even when both Houses of Parliament are in session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: An ordinance can be issued only when Parliament (or at least one House) is not in session.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about precedent as a source of law:
I. Obiter dicta of the Supreme Court are given great weight by lower courts even though they are not strictly binding.
II. The Supreme Court is not bound by its own earlier decisions and can depart from them.
III. A High Court decision binds courts in every state of India.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: A High Court decision binds only the courts subordinate to it; in other states it is persuasive.
options: All of them
II and III only
I and II only
I only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about custom as a source of law is NOT correct?
items.answer: A custom can override a valid statute.
items.markingKey: (d) It is incorrect. A statute prevails over a conflicting custom.
options: The person relying on a custom must prove its existence before the court.
Legislation can abolish or modify a custom.
Hindu law recognises custom; under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 a valid custom can permit a marriage within the prohibited degrees.
A custom can override a valid statute.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Juristic writings carry weight in court.
Reason (R): They explain and systematise the law and are written by recognised experts, though they are not binding.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: they explain and systematise the law and are written by recognised experts, though they are not binding.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on legislation as a source of law and answer the questions that follow.
"Delegated legislation is needed because the legislature lacks time and technical knowledge to make detailed rules. Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines rules made by the executive. Legislation is the most important source of law in modern states."
(i) Which of these is a form of control over delegated legislation? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'ordinance' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The legislature delegates power to the executive to make detailed rules. (1)
items.answer: (i) Judicial review (ii) A law made by the President (Article 123) or a Governor (Article 213) when the legislature is not in session. (iii) The legislature lacks the time and technical expertise to frame every detail and needs flexibility for emergencies.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Judicial review (ii) A law made by the President (Article 123) or a Governor (Article 213) when the legislature is not in session. (iii) The legislature lacks the time and technical expertise to frame every detail and needs flexibility for emergencies.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: Quran – primary source of Muslim law
items.markingKey: (d) Quran – primary source of Muslim law. Qiyas – analogical deduction; Sunna – practice and sayings of the Prophet; Ijma – consensus of jurists are the correct pairs for the others.
options: Qiyas – practice and sayings of the Prophet
Sunna – consensus of jurists
Ijma – analogical deduction
Quran – primary source of Muslim law

items.stem: A claimed custom in Harpreet's area allows a creditor to make a debtor's child work for him until the debt is paid. Which essential of a valid custom is NOT satisfied? Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: Reasonableness and morality; a custom that is unreasonable, immoral or against public policy is not enforced.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for Reasonableness and morality, 1 for the reason (a custom that is unreasonable, immoral or against public policy is not enforced).

items.stem: Which of these is a form of control over delegated legislation?
items.answer: Judicial review
items.markingKey: (c) Judicial review.
options: Presidential pardon
Election petition
Judicial review
Impeachment

items.stem: "The decisions of the Supreme Court bind all courts in India." Examine this statement with reference to precedent as a source of law.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Article 141 declares that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (Article 141 declares that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within India.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about custom as a source of law is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "A custom can override a valid statute."
items.answer: A statute prevails over a conflicting custom.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (A statute prevails over a conflicting custom.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: Article 213 – law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts
items.markingKey: (a) Article 213 – law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts is wrong: Article 213 goes with ordinance-making power of the Governor.
options: Article 213 – law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts
Article 142 – Supreme Court may pass orders for complete justice
Article 123 – ordinance-making power of the President
Article 137 – Supreme Court may review its own judgments
